questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Georgia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Georgia article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Georgia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Georgia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Georgia article.

questions.proof: It is situated on the coast of the Black Sea and borders Russia to the north, Turkey and Armenia to the south, and Azerbaijan to the southeast.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Georgia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Georgia article.

questions.proof: People from Georgia are called Georgians, most of whom speak Georgian as their first language, though some speak Azerbaijani, Armenian, Russian or other languages as well.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was part of the Russian Empire and later Soviet Union between _____ and 1991, but now it is an independent republic.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Georgia article.

questions.proof: It was part of the Russian Empire and later Soviet Union between 1921 and 1991, but now it is an independent republic.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Georgia was part of the Mongol Empire for a century on and off until _____, when King Giorgi V took over.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the fourteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Before 15th century” part of the Georgia article.

questions.proof: Georgia was part of the Mongol Empire for a century on and off until 1334, when King Giorgi V took over.
